clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on apixaban presented with sudden onset mid-back pain after a long flight. Initial workup ruled out pulmonary embolism and he was discharged with mechanical back pain diagnosis. He represented 2 days later with recurrent severe burning pain between the shoulder blades and then next day with urinary retention but preserved lower limb power and sensation. An urgent spinal MRI initially showed thoracic syringomyelia from T1-T5 with lumbar extension. The following day he deteriorated with headache, neck stiffness, vomiting, and lower limb weakness and ataxia leading to hospital admission and cessation of apixaban due to suspicion of spinal hemorrhage. CT head showed possible small subarachnoid hemorrhage. The initial MRI finding was later clarified as spinal subdural haematoma diagnosis. Repeat MRI one month later showed near complete resolution of the haematoma.
